name: archive_extract
description: Extract the members of a zip, tar (plain, gzip, bzip2, xz or zstd), 7z (through the 7z program) or single-file gzip/bzip2/xz/zstd archive into a NEW private directory, bounded and safe against hostile input. Format is read from the bytes. Only member CONTENT is written: a symlink, hard link, device node or FIFO is recorded with its target and never created, nothing lands outside the output directory (files are created exclusively through directory descriptors; an absolute path, a drive letter or '..' is rendered harmless and flagged), and nothing is executed. Every member is one row of members.jsonl in archive order (n is the number the archive-members recipe gives it) with its exact name bytes (name_b64), type, declared and written sizes, the times as stored with their zone said, flags, status and the path it was written to; two members with one name are two files; an encrypted member is counted, never skipped silently and never opened; a compression method this build cannot read is 'unsupported'. A name shaped like a token is withheld from every output channel and kept in withheld-names.jsonl (0600). A member is written as <path>.partial and takes its name only when its size and CRC match what the archive declared; a member that stops, fails or mismatches stays .partial and its row says why. A digest or CRC of a member shorter than 128 bytes is not written. Budgets: max_total_bytes, max_member_bytes, max_members, max_ratio (default 1000), max_depth and max_seconds; a member-level budget skips or cuts that member and goes on, a global one stops the run, names it and gives next_index (run again with from_index and resume true to go on in the same out_dir, which writes a second manifest beside the first). A nested archive is named (looks_like), not opened; one call extracts one level. zstd needs Python 3.14 or the zstd program, else it is reported unsupported. RAR, CAB and ISO are refused by name. A 7z archive with encrypted headers cannot be listed and is refused. Not measured: the content of any member, the archive's authenticity, and whether the archive is the whole of what was acquired. Extracted bytes are evidence content and can hold credentials: when the member list shows credential stores, keys, tokens or browser profiles, run it as a job with secret_output true. The manifest does not force it: an archive of a whole case would make every output sensitive.

path.description: The archive to extract (a file). Its format is read from its bytes, not its name.

out_dir.description: Directory to extract into (default: a new archive_extract-<id> directory beside the tool's other output). Must not already hold files unless resume is true. In a job it must lie under $OUT: give {OUT}/<name>.

resume.description: Go on in an out_dir an earlier run made (with from_index). Nothing already there is replaced; a second members.2.jsonl and receipt.2.json are written.

from_index.description: Start at this member number (default 0): the number a stopped run gave as next_index, and the n of the archive-members recipe.

max_total_bytes.description: Bytes written in all (default 8 GiB, at most 1 TiB); past it the run stops and names where to resume.

max_member_bytes.description: Bytes in one member (default 4 GiB); a longer member is cut, kept as .partial, and the run goes on.

max_members.description: Members handled in this run (default 200000, at most 5000000).

max_ratio.description: Expanded over packed (default 1000): per member for a zip (its directory gives each packed size); over the whole stream for a gzip, bzip2, xz or zstd file or tar, and for a 7z (its output over the archive's size); a plain tar stores its members. A sparse disk image compressed with xz or zstd can pass it; raise it for such an archive on purpose.

max_depth.description: Path components in a member name (default 64); a deeper member is skipped and recorded.

max_seconds.description: Time budget in seconds (default 1500, at most 1700); past it the run stops, and any running 7z is killed.

limit.description: Member rows in the inline page (default 50, at most 1000); members_file has every member.
